question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
trigger: The user requested one final pass against additional editor candidates to validate the cleanest and most performant annotations architecture. Assessment and durable research recording only; no product implementation.
requirements: Compare current source-level ownership, mapping, deletion, projection, rendering and scale mechanics across ProseMirror, Lexical, CKEditor, CodeMirror, Monaco/VS Code, Yjs, Automerge, Quill, Tiptap and current Plite.

Select one document model with independent mounted-view selection, focus, editability, projection, annotation index and paint unless an independent revision or transport job proves another model is required.
Keep application metadata, persistent target, exact-view annotation index and decoration paint as separate lifetimes and authorities.
Keep the public borrowed-target contract scalar and capability-minimal; internal batching or collection mapping must not leak into arbitrary target adapters without a proven public job.
Retain central changed-node and candidate-ID routing and prohibit claims of performance superiority until current, batched and collection candidates pass one matched scale benchmark.

Give deletion policies truthful scope: nearest owns durable fallback and local history recovery; terminal drop owns locally observed transient invalidation and is not promised as a convergent persisted CRDT target.
Preserve explicit owner cleanup, exact-view reads, deterministic overlap, omitted-DOM remount, duplicate-ID failure and typed readers.
Challenge delete, inline, merge and owner-move alternatives before adding a marker collection, interval tree, document mark, second model or new public abstraction.
evidenceReuse: Reused the source-matching September 21 review, its 107/107 core and 64/64 React baselines, deletion probe, consumer census and public-surface findings because the owning product source remained unchanged during this read-only audit. Re-inspected current Plite anchor routing, annotation mapping, persistent snapshot and Comments policy. Added exact current or pinned source evidence for nine external architecture families and official documentation corroboration. No candidate implementation, package replay, browser interaction or matched benchmark was executed.
summary: Pursue and reaffirm the one-model, exact-view-index, separate-paint architecture and the prior API cuts. External source makes the internal performance choice provisional: current node-key routing is the baseline; native batched resolution, a collection-mapped prototype and simpler immutable snapshots must compete in a matched 1/2/4-view scale run before any kernel replacement or fastest-design claim. Keep terminal drop for locally observed transient anchors, but do not describe it as a convergent persisted CRDT target; Comments continues to use nearest. CKEditor, CodeMirror and Monaco supply private algorithm ideas, while their global markers, flat range identity or coarse invalidation are weaker owners for Plate annotations.

reconciliation.question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
reconciliation.reason: Retain its one-model topology, exact-view index, four-lifetime split, borrowed resolve-only target, React ownership, public-surface cuts and terminal local drop target. Narrow the collaboration promise and add a benchmark gate for the private mapping and snapshot kernels; neither refinement reverses the selected public architecture.

alternatives: Delete the annotation engine and inline everything into Comments: reject. Exact-view resolution, changed-node routing and keyed publication are neutral Plite jobs already consumed across the Plite/Plate boundary; inlining relocates them and blocks non-Comments consumers.

Replace anchors and the annotation index with CodeMirror RangeSet or Monaco decorations: reject. Their mapped flat ranges and paint values do not own Plite roots, tree identity, authored projection, saved targets, explicit retained lifetime or terminal policy. Keep them as private benchmark inspirations only.

Adopt CKEditor-style global markers or one live observer per target: reject. Marker queries scan the collection, each live range listens to model operations, and CKEditor explicitly recommends keeping marker counts low.

Persist attachment IDs as Lexical, Automerge or Tiptap document marks: reject for Plate Comments. That puts target identity into document history and serialization while thread data has an external lifecycle. Reopen only for a feature that deliberately chooses collaborative document-owned attachment state.

Share one resolved annotation store across mounted views: reject. Yjs renderer tests and current authored projections prove the same retained target can resolve differently in accepted and proposed views.

Keep the mirrored reviewer document: reject. No independent revision, transport or write authority exists; one model with separate mounted views deletes copied values, selection resets and mirror anchors.

Add public resolveMany, interval-tree or owner-token APIs now: reject. Current external targets need scalar resolve only; the candidate structures are implementation strategies whose value must first be measured.

Rename drop to exact and allow recovery after absence: defer as an unproven third job. Comments uses nearest and current drop callers need terminal local invalidation. Yjs proves that recoverable exact identity needs an explicit collaboration contract, not a casual rename.

Delete the private persistent snapshot trie because it is complex: reject without evidence. Its bounded-copy tests are real; compare wall time and retained heap against a simpler immutable snapshot and delete the loser.

Merge annotation data, target identity and decoration paint: reject. External editors repeatedly need separate metadata, mapped identity, projection-local indexes and viewport paint even when their concrete boundaries differ.
proofLimits: The prior package baselines remain valid observations of current behavior, and current source proves targeted routing and bounded snapshot copying. This pass did not implement the target, run a browser, replay collaboration, measure memory, or compare wall-time kernels. It cannot claim the selected design is fastest. Task design must prove two simultaneous views, projection differences, omitted DOM remount, deterministic overlap, lifecycle cleanup, duplicate IDs and deletion/undo/collaboration boundaries. Benchmark must compare current routing, optional native batch resolution, a collection prototype and simpler snapshots at 1k/10k/100k annotations across one, two and four views.
